findings.reason: The protected source is the conventional stack-based solution for forward-order linked-list addition. The operand stacks, carry loop, and head-prepending result construction are concise, appropriately named, and directly explainable; no inert candidate would materially improve the implementation.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 445 and its Python two-list-to-list surface. The app-local source defines the required minimal ListNode equivalent, accepts the same two forward-order chains as the native method, and returns the same linked result. The modular Reference preserves the non-empty, non-negative, no-leading-zero contract.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064833955. The app and native implementations push the same digits into two stacks, pop and add them with the same carry state, prepend the same result digit on every iteration, and return the same head; only the local ListNode definition, annotations, and Solution wrapper differ.

The 16-, 40-, and 100-digit tiers span 6.25x of the complete legal operand-length domain and exercise traversal, stacks, and result construction. The protected source passed all 10 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 0.98x the reference runtime. A correct O((m + n)^2) head-rescan control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 10.03x.

The Approach now exactly describes the reviewed target's two operand stacks, right-to-left carry propagation, and direct ListNode prepending in both app and native forms. A stale claim that the app collected and reversed ordinary digits was removed. The proof and O(m + n) time and space analysis match the implementation.

The hash-bound Reference was checked against the live public statement. It preserves forward digit order, non-empty operands, leading-zero semantics, all three exact examples without invented explanations, all three constraints, and the follow-up about avoiding input reversal. An independent accessible Mermaid linked-list diagram preserves the relationships and digits shown by the provider image for the first example.
